Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 FY2025 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 FY2025 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Dr. Lena Novak, CTO; Jordan Lee, Chief Revenue Officer; and Taylor Kim, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially due to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 FY2025. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on six key areas: customer mix trends between enterprise and SMB segments, sales efficiency including cycle lengths and conversion rates, CAC trends, product roadmap updates with key initiatives and launches, gross margin performance, and churn analysis with mitigation efforts.

These areas highlight our disciplined approach to scaling in the SaaS landscape, where we're leveraging AI-driven revenue orchestration to help enterprises streamline go-to-market operations, integrating seamlessly with tools like Salesforce, HubSpot, and Marketo. We've seen robust demand across verticals, closing major deals that underscore our land-and-expand model.

To give you more color, I'll turn it over to Mike to walk through the details on our customer mix and other metrics.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. As Sarah noted, we had a strong quarter financially. Revenue for the quarter was $152 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82.5%, and operating income was $38 million.

Let me start with our customer mix, a vital view for grasping our trajectory toward sustainable hypergrowth. In SaaS, enterprise customers bring margin expansion and NRR stability, while SMBs provide topline speed via high-volume, low-friction wins.

In Q2, enterprise customers—those with ACV over $100K—made up 68% of total ARR, up from 58% in Q2 FY2024 and 62% in Q1 FY2025. That's a 17% YoY rise in enterprise ARR share, contributing about $145 million extra to our enterprise revenue base. SMBs, with ACV under $100K, now represent 32% of ARR, down from 42% YoY, but their absolute ARR grew 12% to $68 million, thanks to self-serve channels.

Our blended ACV is $42K, but enterprise new logos averaged $285K, up 22% YoY, while SMB stayed at $28K. Enterprise dollar-based NRR hit 128%, with 35% of growth from upsells into modules like the AI Workflow Engine and CloudForge Security Suite. SMB NRR was 112%, though with higher gross churn at 8% annualized versus 4% for enterprise—highlighting the volume-versus-stickiness dynamic.

Driving this enterprise shift are key tailwinds: we closed eight deals over $5M TCV with Fortune 1000 firms, including a $12M multi-year deal with a top US financial services leader, deploying across 15K seats for compliance automation, all HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II compliant. This echoes ServiceNow's platform scaling or Snowflake's hyperscaler penetrations.

Technically, our Enterprise Gateway from Q1 has transformed things, with zero-trust API ties to Okta, Azure AD, and AWS IAM for seamless SSO and RBAC at petabyte scale. Predictive AI guardrails cut hallucination risks by 40% in agentic workflows, winning RFPs in healthcare and manufacturing. Enterprise sales cycles dropped to 6.5 months from 9, win rates to 42% from 35% YoY.

By region, North America (72% of ARR) shows 75% enterprise mix, supported by our 150-person field sales team alongside Microsoft Dynamics and Workday. EMEA at 65% enterprise benefited from GDPR Phase 2 for DACH and UK financials, though SMB growth slowed to 8% YoY on economic pressures. APAC (18% ARR) balanced at 55% enterprise, up from 45%, with SMB self-serve in India and Indonesia via AWS and Google Cloud marketplaces—ARR per rep up 30%—and 60% enterprise pilot conversions with telcos like Singtel.

We're committed to SMB as a growth engine and upsell source—20% of new enterprise logos started as SMBs. We've enhanced PLG with a freemium tier for CloudForge Essentials, yielding 45K trials and 22% paid conversions. But our goal is 75%+ enterprise mix by FY2026, aiming for $1.2B enterprise ARR via vertical packs like Financial Services Compliance and partners like Snowflake and Databricks for data pipelines.

With IT budgets rebounding—Gartner forecasts 14% SaaS CAGR through 2028—enterprises favor AI platforms. Our 95% enterprise gross margins versus 88% SMB enable 28% R&D spend on multimodal AI agents. This mix sets us for resilient growth, with $3.2B RPO, 68% enterprise.

Next, on sales efficiency—sales cycle length, conversion rates, pipeline velocity, and our Rule of 40 score of 68—outpacing Snowflake and ServiceNow benchmarks.

Average sales cycle shortened to 85 days in Q2, down 18% YoY from 104 and 12% sequentially from 97—seven straight quarters of compression, beating SaaS averages of 95-110 days per Bessemer surveys.

By segment: Enterprise (> $250K ARR) at 112 days, from 135 YoY, via ABM 2.0 with ZoomInfo intent data, cutting 15-20 days in BFSI and retail. Mid-market ($50K-$250K) at 62 days from 78, driven by PLG freemium converting 28% free-to-paid in 30 days, 42% of new logos self-serve like Notion.

Regions: NA at 78 days with AWS Marketplace (15% enterprise wins); EMEA 92 from 118 via localized GDPR AI; APAC 105 on Japan regs, but new Singapore hub and Atlassian-like pricing help.

Key enablers: RevAI lead scoring (92% accuracy on Gong/Outreach data), upping velocity 24%; virtual selling with Loom and sandbox PoCs (3 days vs 2 weeks); usage-based pricing pilots like Snowflake, shortening mid-market by 22%.

Conversion rates: Overall lead-to-close 14.2%, +220 bps YoY, above 10-12% medians. MQL-to-SQL 32% (+4 pts YoY) on inbound/LinkedIn; SQL-to-opp 48% (+6 pts) with multi-threading (3.2 buyers/deal); opp-to-won 42% (+5 pts), expansions at 68%. Enterprise 11.5%, mid-market 22.4% self-serve 31%.

Regions: NA 16.1%, EMEA 12.8% via Accenture, APAC 9.7% targeting 12%. LTV/CAC 4.2x, $1.42M ARR/rep top quartile. Q3 plans: Chorus.ai coaching, Microsoft co-sell, rev ops bundles.

Now, CAC trends, calculated as sales/marketing spend over new customers, targeting LTV/CAC >4:1, payback <9 months.

Blended CAC $428/new customer, -10% seq from $475, -19% YoY from $529—beating 12-15% guidance, like HubSpot's 18% drop.

SMB (68% new logos) $312, -22% YoY, via PLG freemium AI workflows (35% conversion lift, k-factor 1.28, 28% trial-paid vs 18-20% benchmark). Enterprise (32% logos, 62% ARR) $712, -12% from $810, on rep ramp to 4.2 months, Gong AI playbooks, ABM with Marketo/Outreach.

Regions: US (72% new ARR) $415 -21% YoY on SEO (+45%); EMEA $445 -25% on OVHcloud; APAC $512 -8% but 40% MoM SEA trials, Snowflake-style.

Initiatives: $15M no-code AI for SMB CAC <$250, S&M 28% revenue (5.8x content ROI), high-LTV focus (expansions offset 42% churn, Rule 40=62). Q3 $410-420 CAC, $50M brand push.

Gross margins: GAAP 82.5%, +130 bps YoY from 81.2%, +40 bps seq from 82.1%; non-GAAP 84.2%, +160 bps YoY, +50 bps seq.

Scale: Hosting/bandwidth (65% CoR) -18% /petabyte on AWS/Azure/GCP discounts past $450M rev run-rate, Snowflake-style.

Mix: AI modules (22% rev from 14%) at 88% margins, low-GPU tensor runtime; legacy on-prem down to 8% from 75% margins.

MarginForge: AI self-service support -25% costs (65% L1 resolved); 40% data compression -$12M egress; 85% EMEA sovereign clouds.

Regions: US 82.8%, EMEA 86.2% +250 bps, APAC 79.5% maturing. Q4 non-GAAP 85.2% on zero-ETL, multi-cloud hedges.

Churn: Logo 4.2% -150 bps YoY from 5.7%; dollar 3.8% -120 bps; NRR 112% +4 pts, expansions $18M (22% ARR), beating HubSpot/Zendesk medians.

Drivers: Econ 42% (SMB 28%, EMEA 35%); competition 31% (Teams 18%, AI lag 13%); fit/friction 20% (SMB 15%, APAC 25%); support 7%.

Cohorts: Q1'25 2.1% dollar churn at 6 months vs 5.2%.

Mitigations ($25M invest): CS 1:150 ratio, ML health score 94% accuracy, 1,200 saves $12M ARR (Gainsight-like); ForgeAI 40% TTV cut, usage pricing -22% SMB churn; ForgeLocal compliance -30%; dynamic pricing 96% renewals, $45M expansions.

Land-expand 68% from modules, NRR to 115%+.

We continue investing in R&D for innovation. Cash position strong at $450M, flexibility for acquisitions. Updating full-year guidance: revenue $590M to $610M.

Now, over to Lena for tech update.

Dr. Lena Novak:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we advanced our AI capabilities, integrating them deeply into the CloudForge core platform. Adoption of AI-powered features is surging, boosting user engagement and customer outcomes. We've enhanced security and scalability for enterprise demands, including zero-trust integrations and predictive guardrails reducing risks by 40%.

Now, Taylor will update on product roadmap.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Lena. We've prioritized user experience, announcing ForgeAI Insights 2.0—next-gen predictive analytics with GPT-4o-like LLMs and zero-knowledge ML, cutting MTTR 65%, 42% ARR activation, $18M incremental ARR. Resonates in finance/healthcare.

Unified Workflow Orchestrator: low-code 150+ integrations (AWS Bedrock, etc.), 35% new logos bundle it, churn <3%.

NPS 68 +12 pts, PLG 28% new ARR.

Forward: Forge Forward—AI Agents Q3 (Llama 3.1 RAG, 95% accurate, 30-40% waste cut, 200-300 bps NRR); verticals (Industrial IoT Q4 OPC UA/5G, Commerce AI Nov 92% forecast); Federated Edge sovereign clouds Singapore/São Paulo.

Regions: NA 65% ARR $920M NRR 130%; EMEA 55% growth $145M; APAC/LATAM 45% $110M, Bengaluru R&D.

$200B TAM 22% CAGR, ahead of Salesforce/Oracle. Q3 $65-70M new ARR from launches.

Now, back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions: Press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Emily Wong with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Wong:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, and how it compares to your initial expectations?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Emily. ForgeAI has been transformative for growth, contributing 22% of revenue and driving 35% of enterprise ARR expansions. Attach rates are at 42% across the base, with 68% in new enterprise logos—well above our 30% initial target. This exceeds expectations by 20%, accelerating land-and-expand and boosting pipeline velocity.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Raj Patel:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, and what are your key target markets?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Raj. International expansion is core, with APAC now 18% of ARR, up significantly. We're targeting telcos like Singtel, financials in India/Indonesia via marketplaces, and manufacturing in Japan. Plans include Singapore hub, localized LLMs/pricing, sovereign clouds, and 20% Bengaluru R&D for 40% YoY growth, outpacing regional averages.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan.

Lisa Chen:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, and what are your strategies to improve customer retention?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, Lisa. Churn management leverages proactive CS with ML health scores (94% accuracy), saving $12M ARR. Logo churn 4.2%, dollar 3.8%, NRR trending to 112% from 108% YoY. Strategies: ForgeAI for 40% faster value, usage pricing -22% SMB churn, regional compliance zones -30%, dynamic renewals at 96%. Targeting sub-3.5% dollar churn.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
